gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Synology DS225+ ships with 2 GB of RAM while Virtual Machine Manager runs VMs only on NAS units with more than 2 GB, so a stock DS225+ can't run a Home Assistant OS VM until the D4NS01-4G module is added.
standout_why: I compared against the cited Synology VMM 7.4 spec, QNAP's USB passthrough FAQ, UGREEN KB 642 and 911, and the SmartHomeJunkie DXP4800 GT guide. The Synology spec gives the 'more than 2 GB' rule but names no models and gives no stock RAM. ChatGPT recommended the DS923+/DS925+ and never named the DS225+. None of the cited pages connects the rule to the DS225+'s 2 GB. Of the top results, GitHub #162157 (Synology VMM drops the ZBT-2 during its firmware flash) appeared in ChatGPT's results but was not cited, so that finding is only partly new. None of the rival pages mentions that UGREEN's DH-series NAS units can't run VMs at all.
decides: Our current page lists the DS225+ as a Synology pick. Its row should say the 2 GB unit can't run a VM as shipped and needs Synology's D4NS01-4G module (6 GB total). The DS925+ (4 GB) and the QNAP TS-264 (8 GB, above Virtualization Station's 4 GB minimum) work as shipped. The UGREEN DH2300 and DH4300 Plus, which Dealectric lists, should be marked unable to run Home Assistant OS as a VM. A buyer of the Home Assistant ZBT-2 stick who plans to use Synology VMM should be told to flash the stick on a desktop first.

findings.label: Minimum NAS memory to run any VM
findings.value: VMs run only on Synology NAS with more than 2 GB of memory; VM data must be on a Btrfs volume
findings.source_title: Virtual Machine Manager Technical Specifications | Synology Inc.
findings.note: Quoted: 'Virtual machines can run only on Synology NAS devices with more than 2 GB of memory.' 'Virtual machine data can be stored only on Btrfs volumes.'

findings.label: USB passthrough scope
findings.value: USB 2.0/3.0 passthrough for VMs; not supported on Virtual DSM
findings.source_title: Virtual Machine Manager Technical Specifications | Synology Inc.
findings.note: The page gives no per-VM limit on USB devices. Disk image import is listed as IMG, VMDK, VDI, VHD, VHDX and QCOW2, so the HAOS KVM .qcow2 image can be imported.

findings.label: Installed / maximum RAM and compatible module
findings.value: 2 GB DDR4 non-ECC installed; 6 GB maximum (2 GB + 4 GB); module D4NS01-4G
findings.note: 2 GB is not 'more than 2 GB', so the stock unit is below VMM's VM threshold. Adding the D4NS01-4G gives 6 GB. CPU Intel Celeron J4125, two USB 3.2 Gen 1 ports, 2 recommended VM instances, 3-year warranty.

findings.label: Virtualization Station memory requirement vs installed
findings.value: At least 4 GB RAM required; TS-264-8G ships with 8 GB (max 16 GB); 4 suggested VMs
findings.note: Spec lists Virtualization Station for QTS 6.1.0 and QuTS hero h6.1.0. CPU Celeron N5095. USB: 2× USB 2.0 and 2× USB 3.2 Gen 2 Type-A. 3-year warranty.

findings.label: USB 3.2 Gen 1 passthrough condition
findings.value: Depends on guest OS (Linux kernel 3.4.6 or later listed); if the guest lacks support, use a host USB 2.0 port
findings.source_title: Does Virtualization Station support USB 3.2 Gen 1 passthrough? | QNAP (US)
findings.note: Last modified 2024-07-10. No NAS model, chipset or device-count exclusions are stated. The TS-264 has two USB 2.0 ports available for the fallback.

findings.label: VM image formats and firmware requirement
findings.value: Images offered: KVM/Proxmox .qcow2, VirtualBox .vdi, VMware ESXi .ova; HAOS requires UEFI (non-Secure-Boot OVMF); minimum 2 GB RAM, 2 vCPUs
findings.note: Home Assistant's own Synology and QNAP sections describe Docker/Container installs, not HAOS VMs. It says its Synology container instructions 'do not correctly configure the container to access the USB devices' (Z-Wave and Bluetooth sticks named). Both brands therefore need the VM route for HAOS with a USB stick.

findings.label: First-time firmware install on HAOS in Synology VMM
findings.value: Fails with 'Failed to install firmware' / 'Failed to probe running application type'; stick not detected again until reattached or VM restarted
findings.source_title: ZBT-2 first-time installation fails during recommended setup procedure on virtualised HAOS · Issue #162157 · home-assistant/core
findings.note: Reporter used a Synology RS1221+; another reporter a DS923+. A user's analysis says the ZBT-2 resets during flashing and VMM drops the passthrough without reconnecting. No maintainer has replied. Issue still open after a 2026-10-17 comment. User-reported workarounds: flash the stick on a desktop with the Nabu Casa toolbox, or reboot the VM from the hypervisor.

findings.label: Virtual machine support
findings.value: None: Dong Ngo lists 'no virtual machine support'; Rockchip RK3588 ARM, 8 GB RAM, not expandable
findings.source_title: UGREEN NASync DH4300 Plus review | Dong Knows Tech (Dong Ngo, 2025-09-04)
findings.note: Named reviewer used as fallback; the maker's FAQ page returned HTTP 429 on three tries. Docker is available. This excludes the DH4300 Plus, which Dealectric lists, from a HAOS VM build.
